Prealgebra · Lesson 11.5

Perimeter

Solve this lesson →All lessons

You already know the perimeter is the distance all the way around a figure, the total you get by adding up its sides. Now we make that quick. We will build formulas for rectangles and squares, deduce missing side lengths on figures that are only partly labelled, and see what cutting a piece out of a shape does to its boundary, which is sometimes nothing at all.

Problem
In the diagram above is a rectangle 12 units wide and 7 units tall. Find its perimeter. Give the number of units.
Show a hint
  • The perimeter is the distance all the way around. A rectangle has two widths and two heights, so the shortcut is P=2(l+w)P=2(l+w).
  • Add the width and the height first, then double that sum.
Show the full solution
Add the width and the height, then double. P=2(l+w)=2(12+7)=2×19=38P=2(l+w)=2(12+7)=2×19=38 The perimeter is 3838​ units. Doubling works because a rectangle has two equal widths and two equal heights, so you never need to add all four sides.
Problem
In the diagram above is a square with side 9. Find its perimeter. Give the number of units.
Show a hint
  • A square has four sides, and they are all the same length. So instead of adding four different numbers, you can add the same number four times.
  • That repeated addition is just multiplication. Multiply the side length by 4.
Show the full solution
A square's four sides are all equal, so its perimeter is 4s4s. With a side of 9 that gives P=4×9=36.P=4×9=36. The perimeter is 3636​ units.
Problem
The figure above is a rectangle with length 1313 and an unknown width. Its perimeter is 4040. Find the width. Give the number of units.
Show a hint
  • The perimeter 2(l+w)2(l+w) is made of two lengths and two widths, so half of it is exactly one length plus one width. Start by halving 4040.
  • Half the perimeter is 402=20240​=20, and that equals one length plus one width. You already know the length is 1313, so subtract it out to uncover the width.
Show the full solution
Half the perimeter is one length plus one width, and half of 4040 is 2020. The length is 1313, so the width is 20−13=7.20−13=7​. Halving first is faster than writing 2(13+w)=402(13+w)=40 and unwinding it, though both get there.
Problem
In the diagram above is a square whose perimeter is 4848. Find the length of one side. Give the number of units.
Show a hint
  • A square has four equal sides, so the perimeter is 4s4s. You know the perimeter and want the side.
  • Undo the multiplication by 4. Divide the perimeter by 4 to get one side.
Show the full solution
A square's four sides are equal, so its perimeter is 4s4s. Here 4s=484s=48, so divide both sides by 4 to get one side. s=484=12s=448​=12​ One side is 12 units.
Key idea
Perimeter of a rectangle and a square. A rectangle has two lengths and two widths, so add one of each and double it, P=2(l+w)P=2(l+w). A square has four equal sides, so P=4sP=4s. Each formula also works backward. Half the perimeter is one length plus one width, l+w=P2l+w=2P​, so subtract the side you know to get the other. One side of a square is a quarter of its perimeter, s=P4s=4P​.
Problem
The diagram above shows an L-shaped figure with its six sides marked 99, 33, 55, 33, 44, and 66. Find its perimeter. Give the number of units.
Show a hint
  • The perimeter of any figure is the total distance around it, so it's just the sum of all its sides. Here every side you need is already marked.
  • Add the six marked lengths together, going once around the figure. 9+3+5+3+4+69+3+5+3+4+6.
Show the full solution
Every side is marked, so add all six. 9+3+5+3+4+6=309+3+5+3+4+6=30​ The perimeter is 3030 units. An L-shape has no formula, and it does not need one, since perimeter is always just the trip around.
Problem
The figure above is an L-shaped room. Its six walls measure 1616, 1010, 77, 44, 99, and 66. A builder wants to run baseboard trim all the way around the floor, along every wall. Find the total length of baseboard needed, which is the perimeter of the room. Give the number of units.
Show a hint
  • Baseboard runs along every wall with no gaps, so its total length is the perimeter, the sum of all six sides.
  • Every side is already marked on the figure above, so no side needs to be deduced. Add all six lengths together.
Show the full solution
Baseboard runs along every wall with no gaps, so its length is the perimeter. All six walls are marked, so add them. 16+10+7+4+9+6=5216+10+7+4+9+6=52​ The builder needs 5252 units of baseboard.
Problem
In the diagram above is a staircase figure with all eight of its sides marked. The bottom and the left side are each 66, and the six little step sides are each 22. Add up every side to find the perimeter. Give the number of units.
Show a hint
  • The perimeter is the sum of all eight sides. Read each length off the diagram and lay them out in one long sum before you add.
  • There is a shortcut worth noticing. A staircase that only steps outward wraps the same distance as the rectangle that boxes it in, so the three horizontal steps together span the same width as the 66 at the bottom, and the three vertical steps span the same height as the 66 on the left.
Show the full solution
Add all eight sides, the 66 along the bottom, the 66 up the left, and the six step sides of 22. 6+2+2+2+2+2+2+6=246+2+2+2+2+2+2+6=24​ The three horizontal steps span the same width as the bottom 66, and the three vertical steps the same height as the left 66, so the outline wraps as far as the 66-by-66 box around it, 2(6+6)=242(6+6)=24.
Key idea
Composite figures with unlabelled sides. A composite figure, like an L, is made of rectangles joined together. Its perimeter is the sum of all its sides. When a side is left unmarked, find it from the sides opposite it. The horizontal pieces along the top add to the same width as the bottom, and the vertical pieces on one side add to the same height as the other. So a missing length is the matching total minus the pieces you know.
Problem
In the diagram above is a staircase figure. Only its overall width 1212 along the bottom and its overall height 88 up the left side are marked, and every other side is left blank. Find its perimeter. Give the number of units.
Show a hint
  • A staircase only steps outward, so slide each horizontal piece up and each vertical piece across until the outline snaps onto the smallest rectangle that would just contain it. Nothing about the total length changes.
  • That bounding rectangle is 1212 wide and 88 tall, so its perimeter is 2(W+H)2(W+H). Read off WW and HH from the two marked sides.
Show the full solution
Slide every horizontal step up to the top and every vertical step out to the right. The staircase only steps outward, so nothing overlaps and no length is lost, and the outline matches the 1212 by 88 box around it. P=2(W+H)=2(12+8)=40P=2(W+H)=2(12+8)=40​ The individual step sizes never matter, which is why you were not given them.
Problem
The diagram above is a rectangle 14 by 9 with a small rectangular piece cut out of one corner. Its six sides, going around, are 1414, 77, 33, 22, 1111, and 99. Find the perimeter. Give the number of units.
Show a hint
  • A corner notch pushes the boundary in and then straight back out. The two little sides you gained replace exactly the length you gave up, so the perimeter matches the full rectangle the piece was cut from.
  • That full rectangle is 14 by 9, so its perimeter is 2(14+9)2(14+9). Or add the six marked sides straight off the figure and check they agree.
Show the full solution
Add the six marked sides. 14+7+3+2+11+9=4614+7+3+2+11+9=46​ That matches 2(14+9)2(14+9), the perimeter of the full 1414 by 99 rectangle. A corner notch steps in and back out, so its two new sides cover exactly the edge they replaced.
Problem
In the diagram above is a rectangle 12 units wide and 8 units tall, with a slot cut into its top edge 3 units wide and 2 units deep. Find the perimeter. Give the number of units.
Show a hint
  • Start with the plain rectangle, before the slot. Its perimeter is 2(l+w)2(l+w), so 2(12+8)2(12+8).
  • The slot's 3-unit width is already part of the top edge, so cutting it costs nothing there. What it adds are the two new vertical walls of the slot, each 2 units deep. Add twice the depth to the rectangle's perimeter.
Show the full solution
The full rectangle has perimeter 2(12+8)=402(12+8)=40. The slot's two side walls are new, each 2 units deep, so they add 2×2=42×2=4. 40+4=4440+4=44​ The slot's 3-unit width costs nothing, since the strip taken off the top edge comes back as the slot's floor. Only the depth counts, and it counts twice.
Key idea
Staircases, notches, and slots. A staircase that only steps outward has the same perimeter as the smallest box around it, 2(W+H)2(W+H), since sliding each step out to the edge adds no length. Cutting a corner notch also leaves the perimeter unchanged, since the two new edges total the same as the two removed. A slot cut into an edge is different. It adds twice its depth, since the boundary goes in and back out.
Problem
The rectangle in the diagram above has length (x+3)(x+3) and width 2x2x, and its perimeter is 3030. Find xx. Give the value of xx.
Show a hint
  • Perimeter of a rectangle is 2(l+w)2(l+w). Add the length and width, double it, and set that equal to 3030.
  • Once you have 2((x+3)+2x)=302((x+3)+2x)=30, divide both sides by 22 first. That leaves a simple equation in xx to solve.
Show the full solution
Perimeter is 2(l+w)2(l+w), so 2((x+3)+2x)=302((x+3)+2x)=30. Divide both sides by 22 to get (x+3)+2x=15(x+3)+2x=15, which is 3x+3=153x+3=15. Then 3x=123x=12, so x=4x=4​.
Key idea
Perimeter as an equation. When the sides are written as expressions in xx, the perimeter is still their sum, so add the expressions just like numbers, combining like terms. A side of x+3x+3 and a side of 2x2x together give 3x+33x+3. If you are told the total perimeter, set your expression equal to it and solve for xx.
Fun fact
Legend says that when Queen Dido founded the city of Carthage, she was allowed only as much land as a single oxhide could surround. So she cut the hide into one long, thin strip to make the longest boundary she could, then laid it in a great arc against the sea to enclose the most land possible. It is an ancient echo of a real idea, that for a fixed perimeter a rounded shape holds the most area.
Problem
In the diagram above is a triangle whose three sides are xx, (x+2)(x+2), and (x+4)(x+4), and its perimeter is 2727. Find the LONGEST side. Give the number of units.
Show a hint
  • Perimeter is the sum of all three sides, so add the three labels and set that equal to 2727.
  • Combine the xx terms to get a single equation in xx, solve it, then plug back into the longest label, x+4x+4.
Show the full solution
The perimeter is the sum of the three sides, so add the labels and set the total to 2727.x+(x+2)+(x+4)=27x+(x+2)+(x+4)=27Combine like terms to get 3x+6=273x+6=27, so 3x=213x=21 and x=7x=7. The longest side is x+4x+4, which is 7+4=117+4=11​.
Problem
In the diagram above is a U-shaped figure with a deep slot cut down from the top. Its eight sides, going around, are 1212, 88, 44, 55, 44, 55, 44, and 88. Find its perimeter. Give the number of units.
Show a hint
  • Perimeter is the whole trip around the outside, so you just add every side you walk along. The slot doesn't change that rule. Both walls of the slot are part of the outside, so both get counted.
  • Add all eight numbers on the diagram. Group them however is easiest, and make sure both 55-unit slot walls are in your sum.
Show the full solution
Add all eight sides. 12+8+4+5+4+5+4+8=5012+8+4+5+4+5+4+8=50​ Both 55-unit walls of the slot count. You walk down one and back up the other, so a slot adds two lengths to the trip, not one.

Practice these ideas

Practice
In the diagram above is a rectangle 15 units wide and 8 units tall. Find its perimeter. Give the number of units.
Show the solution
Add the width and the height, then double. 2(15+8)=2×23=462(15+8)=2×23=46​ The perimeter is 4646 units. The doubling works because opposite sides of a rectangle are equal.
Practice
The diagram above shows a square with each side 11 units long. Find its perimeter. Give the number of units.
Show the solution
A square is four copies of the same side, so its perimeter is 4s4s. With s=11s=11, 4×11=44.4×11=44. The perimeter is 4444​ units.
Practice
The rectangle in the diagram above is 16 units long, and its perimeter is 50. Find its width. Give the number of units.
Show the solution
A rectangle's perimeter is 2(l+w)2(l+w), so half of it is exactly one length plus one width. Half of 5050 is 2525, and that equals the length plus the width. The length is 1616, so the width is 25−16=9.25−16=9​.
Practice
The diagram above shows a square whose perimeter is 5252. Find the length of one side. Give the number of units.
Show the solution
All four sides of a square are equal, so the perimeter is 4s4s. Setting that equal to 5252 and dividing by 44 gives the side.s=524=13s=452​=13​
Practice
In the diagram above is an L-shape with its six sides marked 88, 44, 55, 33, 33, and 77. Find its perimeter. Give the number of units.
Show the solution
Add the six marked sides. 8+4+5+3+3+7=308+4+5+3+3+7=30​ The perimeter is 3030 units. There is no formula for an L-shape, so walk once around and add each side as you pass it.
Practice
In the diagram above is a staircase figure with its six sides marked 88, 33, 44, 33, 44, and 66. Find its perimeter. Give the number of units.
Show the solution
Perimeter is the total distance around the figure, so add all six marked sides. 8+3+4+3+4+6=288+3+4+3+4+6=28​ The perimeter is 2828 units.
Practice
The staircase in the diagram above steps outward from bottom to top, and only two lengths are marked: the total width 1010 along the bottom and the total height 77 up the left side. Find its perimeter. Give the number of units.
Show the solution
A staircase that only steps outward wraps the same distance as the smallest rectangle around it. The horizontal pieces up top add to the same 1010 as the bottom, and the vertical pieces add to the same 77 as the left side. P=2(10+7)=34P=2(10+7)=34​ The individual step sizes never come into it, which is why you were only given the two totals.
Practice
The figure above is a 12-by-8 rectangle with a small notch cut out of one corner. Find its perimeter. Give the number of units.
Show the solution
A notch does not change the perimeter, so use the full 12-by-8 rectangle. 2(12+8)=402(12+8)=40​ The two short pieces the notch removes from the outer edges are exactly replaced by the two sides of the notch itself, so the trip around comes out the same.
Practice
The figure above is an 11-by-7 rectangle with a slot 2 units wide and 3 units deep cut straight into its top edge. Find the perimeter of this figure. Give the number of units.
Show the solution
The full rectangle is 2(11+7)=362(11+7)=36, and the slot adds twice its depth for its two walls, 2×3=62×3=6. 36+6=4236+6=42​ The slot's 2-unit width changes nothing, since the strip taken off the top edge comes back as the slot's floor.
Practice
In the diagram above is a rectangle whose length is (x+5)(x+5) and whose width is 3x3x. Its perimeter is 4242. Find the value of xx. Give the value of xx.
Show the solution
The perimeter is 2(l+w)2(l+w), so one length plus one width is half of it, 2121. That gives (x+5)+3x=21.(x+5)+3x=21. Combine the xx terms to get 4x+5=214x+5=21, so 4x=164x=16 and x=4x=4​.
Practice
In the diagram above is an isosceles triangle whose sides are labelled xx, 2x2x, and 2x2x, and its perimeter is 4040. Find the length of the longest side. Give the number of units.
Show the solution
The perimeter is the sum of all three sides, so x+2x+2x=5xx+2x+2x=5x. Setting that equal to the given perimeter gives 5x=40,x=8.5x=40,x=8. The longest side is 2x=2(8)=162x=2(8)=16​.
Practice
In the diagram above is an L-shaped patio. Its walls, going around, measure 15,9,6,4,9,15,9,6,4,9, and 55 units. Find the perimeter of the patio. Give the number of units.
Show the solution
Perimeter is the total distance around the figure, so add all six walls in order. 15+9+6+4+9+5=4815+9+6+4+9+5=48​ The patio's perimeter is 4848 units.
Practice
The diagram above shows a U-shape with its sides marked 14,9,5,6,4,6,5,914,9,5,6,4,6,5,9. Find its perimeter. Give the number of units.
Show the solution
The perimeter of any figure is the sum of all its sides, so read the eight marked lengths off the diagram and add them up. 14+9+5+6+4+6+5+9=5814+9+5+6+4+6+5+9=58​ The perimeter is 5858 units.
